insights.title: Insights & Methodology 📚
insights.subtitle: Understand what each page reveals, how analytics are calculated, and system limitations. Reference for importing your data and making the most of the dashboard.

summary.patterns: Patterns: Overview, Timeline, Heatmap, Temporal Analysis, Genres, AI features, and date filters reveal your listening habits.
summary.calculations: Calculations: PostgreSQL aggregations (daily/weekly/monthly), global stats, genre cascade (Track → ARTIST_TO_GENRE_MAP → Unknown), and CSV/JSON/PDF exports.
summary.limitations: Limitations: Genre mapping coverage, Last.fm-only data sources, estimated listen time, query performance with large datasets, and artist/track name normalization.
summary.architecture: Architecture: Next.js 14, PostgreSQL + Prisma, Redis-ready cache, Recharts, and Last.fm import via scripts or API.

overview.title: Overview
overview.paragraph: The /dashboard/overview page displays your global stats with comparison to the previous period: total listens, unique artists and tracks, total time. A recent evolution chart (area chart) and top genres complete the picture.

timeline.title: Timeline and Temporal Trends
timeline.paragraph: The /dashboard/timeline and /dashboard/genres/trends pages reveal listening cycles with aggregation by day, week or month:
timeline.li1: Weekly cycles: Days of the week when you listen the most
timeline.li2: Seasonal variations: Monthly evolution of habits
timeline.li3: Genre trends: Genres on the rise or decline over the period (first vs second half comparison)

heatmap.title: Listening Heatmap
heatmap.paragraph: The /dashboard/heatmap page displays a GitHub-style calendar with listening intensity per day. It identifies your most active days and distribution by day of the week.

temporal.title: Advanced Temporal Analysis
temporal.paragraph: The /dashboard/temporal-analysis page details your listening patterns: listens by day of the week (Monday-Sunday), by hour of the day, and identifies peak moments (day and hour when you listen the most).

genres.title: Genre Diversity and Preferences
genres.paragraph: The /dashboard/genres and /genres/trends pages reveal the extent of your musical palette: dominant genres, temporal evolution, and genre diversity. Metrics (unique artists, unique tracks) show the balance between repetition and exploration.

ai.title: AI-Powered Insights
ai.paragraph: Several pages use AI to analyze your listening:
ai.li1: /dashboard/ai-insights: Natural language insights generated from your data (optional, requires Groq)
ai.li2: /dashboard/taste-profile: Explains your musical taste in plain language
ai.li3: /dashboard/taste-evolution: Week-to-week taste changes with AI context
ai.li4: /dashboard/when-will-i-listen: Predicts your most likely listening time slot and genre

dateRange.title: Date Range Filter
dateRange.paragraph: The filter bar at the top lets you focus on specific periods: 7 days, 30 days, year-to-date, or all time. All dashboard pages respect this filter. Exports (CSV, JSON, PDF) also use the selected period.

aggregations.title: Temporal Aggregations
aggregations.paragraph: Aggregations use native PostgreSQL SQL queries for optimal performance:
aggregations.li1: Daily: DATE(played_at) to group by day
aggregations.li2: Weekly: DATE_TRUNC('week', played_at) to group by week (Monday-Sunday)
aggregations.li3: Monthly: TO_CHAR(played_at, 'YYYY-MM') to group by month
aggregations.li4: Counts: Use of COUNT(*) and COUNT(DISTINCT ...) for aggregated metrics

stats.title: Global Statistics
stats.paragraph: Overview statistics are calculated as follows:
stats.li1: Total listens: Total count of records in the Listen table
stats.li2: Unique artists: Distinct count of artist_id via listened tracks
stats.li3: Unique tracks: Distinct count of track_id
stats.li4: Total time: Sum of track durations (in seconds) for all listens

genres.title: Genre Distribution
genres.paragraph: Genres follow a cascade resolution with priority:
genres.li1: 1. Track.genre: Genre stored on the track (from Last.fm on import or via fetch-track-genres.js script using Last.fm, MusicBrainz, Spotify)
genres.li2: 2. ARTIST_TO_GENRE_MAP: Static manual mapping by artist name (fallback if Track.genre is null)
genres.li4: Listens are aggregated by resolved genre; percentages are calculated on total listens

export.title: Data Export
export.paragraph: Exports are available in the filter bar (CSV, JSON, PDF icons):
export.li1: CSV: All listens with Date, Artist, Title, Genre, Source (period filters applied)
export.li2: JSON: Aggregated statistics (overview, timeline, genres) in structured format
export.li3: PDF: Custom annual report with charts and top artists/tracks per year

genreMapping.title: Genre Mapping
genreMapping.limitation: The ARTIST_TO_GENRE_MAP fallback only covers a handful of popular artists. Tracks without genre in the database remain classified as "Unknown" until the fetch-track-genres.js script has been run.
genreMapping.impact: Some artists/tracks may appear as "Unknown", reducing the fineness of genre analysis.
genreMapping.solution: Current solution: Run node scripts/fetch-track-genres.js with LASTFM_API_KEY to enrich genres via Last.fm, MusicBrainz and Spotify (optional).

dataSources.title: Data Sources
dataSources.limitation: Currently: Last.fm is supported (real API when LASTFM_API_KEY is configured, mock otherwise for development).
dataSources.impact: Data may be incomplete if you mainly use Spotify, YouTube Music or other platforms without Last.fm history.
dataSources.solution: Future extensions: Spotify support (OAuth required), YouTube Music, etc.

listenTime.title: Listen Time Calculation
listenTime.limitation: Total listening time is estimated by summing track durations, without accounting for interruptions or partial listens.
listenTime.impact: Calculated time may overestimate actual listening time if tracks are often interrupted or partially listened.
listenTime.solution: Possible improvement: Use playback progress data if available in sources.

queryPerformance.title: Query Performance
queryPerformance.limitation: Trade-off: Complex aggregations require loading listens into memory for calculations.
queryPerformance.impact: Performance may degrade with very large datasets (millions of listens).
queryPerformance.solution: Possible optimizations: Materialized views, additional indexes, or asynchronous calculations for large data.

dataNormalization.title: Data Normalization
dataNormalization.limitation: Normalization of artist and track names depends on exact string matching.
dataNormalization.impact: Name variants (e.g. "The Weeknd" vs "Weeknd") may create duplicate entries in statistics.
dataNormalization.solution: Possible improvement: Use MusicBrainz identifiers (MBID) or fuzzy matching algorithms for deduplication.

stack.title: Technology Stack
stack.li1: Backend: Next.js 14 (App Router) with API Routes
stack.li3: Cache: Redis ready (optional, REDIS_URL); TanStack Query for client-side cache
stack.li4: Frontend: React 18, TanStack Query v5, Tailwind CSS, Sonner (toasts)

model.title: Data Model
model.li1: Artist: name, nameLower (case-insensitive search), MBID, imageUrl
model.li2: Track: title, artist, duration, genre (Last.fm or script), MBID
model.li3: Listen: timestamp (playedAt), source (lastfm), link to Track

import.title: Data Import
import.li1: Last.fm: npm run lastfm:update or API POST /api/lastfm/import (requires LASTFM_API_KEY and LASTFM_USER)
import.li2: Genres: node scripts/fetch-track-genres.js to enrich genres via Last.fm/MusicBrainz/Spotify

whatIs.title: What is this?
whatIs.paragraph: Apple Music Analytics is a personal dashboard that visualizes your music listening habits. It uses your history from Last.fm to show you stats, trends, and insights about how you listen.

whyLastfm.title: Why Last.fm instead of Apple Music?
whyLastfm.paragraph: The official Apple Music API requires a paid developer membership and has usage-based costs. Last.fm offers a free API for personal use, making it an affordable way to track your listening history.

whatIsLastfm.title: What is Last.fm?
whatIsLastfm.paragraph: Last.fm is a music discovery service that tracks what you listen to across streaming platforms (Apple Music, Spotify, etc.). When you connect Last.fm to your Apple Music account, it records each track you play — artist, title, and timestamp — and stores this history on your Last.fm profile. This project fetches that history and stores it locally for analytics.

workflow.title: How does the data get here?

steps.step1: Listen to music — Use Apple Music (or any supported app) on your phone as usual.
steps.step2: Last.fm scrobbling — Last.fm is linked to your Apple Music account and automatically records each listen.
steps.step3: Sync scrobbles — You manually open the Last.fm app on your phone and scan for new scrobbles to transfer data from Apple Music to Last.fm.
steps.step4: Update the database — Run the sync command (or use the API) to fetch new scrobbles and update your local database.
steps.step5: Dashboard reflects data — Once the database is updated, the dashboard shows your latest listening stats.
steps.step6: Outdated data? — If the dashboard looks stale, it usually means the database hasn't been updated yet with new scrobbles from Last.fm.
